- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), particularly if recent price action shows mean reversion; add 1–3% to forecast to account for downward momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment spikes; if sentiment jumps to 1.00 followed by a drop, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overshoot.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows sharp decline after a peak, adjust downward by 5–10% if sentiment was bullish in prior 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price declines over 3–5 days, assume mean reversion and reduce forecast by 2–4% per day of negative sentiment drift.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), use midpoint of recent 5-day average as baseline; avoid extreme forecasts unless sentiment is >0.80.
- Avoid forecasting above 75% of recent 18-day high unless sentiment is >0.80 and no recent price correction; cap forecasts at 75% of recent high for safety.
